expected: 10 males and 10 females with ages from 24 to 84 and a median of 57
quote: The cohort consisted of 10 males and 10 females with ages ranging from 24 to 84 years old and median age of 57 years

expected: a median of 196000 CD45 positive events with a 25th to 75th percentile of 100000 to 278000
quote: Approximately 1 million cells were stained for each panel and a median of 196,000 CD45+ events collected (25th-75th percentile: 100,000-278,000 events)

short_name: The order of the major populations
expected: T cells then monocytes then B cells then NK cells then dendritic cells then HSPC
quote: Most frequent cell subtype populations observed were, in order, T cells, monocytes, B cells, NK cells, DCs, and HSPCs

short_name: Memory T cells rise with age
expected: a positive correlation between the memory T cell frequency and donor age
quote: It is well established that the memory T cell population increases with increasing age in humans, likely due to response to viral infection (in particular CMV), and this trend was reproduced in our cohort using both scRNA-Seq and flow cytometry

short_name: The second aspiration agrees with the first
expected: the two aspirations of a donor agree by flow cytometry
quote: These biological replicates showed good concordance by flow cytometry but showed variation by scRNA-Seq particularly in lower frequency cell subsets, likely from sampling error

short_name: Mass cytometry agrees with flow cytometry
expected: a strong correlation between the two technologies on the CD4 and CD8 T cell subsets
quote: Correlation between mass cytometry and flow cytometry for CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocyte subsets was strong, as shown in Figure 3B

short_name: T cells are the most frequent population
expected: T cells hold the largest share of CD45 positive cells
quote: Most frequent cell subtype populations observed were, in order, T cells, monocytes, B cells, NK cells, DCs, and HSPCs

short_name: Every donor was measured on five panels
expected: five stained panels and one unstained control for each of the 22 samples
quote: Thirteen-color flow cytometry using 5 customized panels (T, B, and NK cells; monocytes; and DCs see Supplemental Table 1) designed to allow deep immunophenotyping of the predominant cell populations found in human bone marrow was performed on all samples
